results.title: Benchmarking Methodology for AI Inference Serving Network Fabrics
results.summary: IETF draft defining terminology, methodology, and a four-tier KPI framework (TTFT, inter-token latency, goodput, fabric-level metrics) for benchmarking Ethernet-based AI inference network fabrics, covering RDMA KV-cache transfers and disaggregated prefill/decode.

results.title: NetKV: Network-Aware Decode Instance Selection for Disaggregated LLM Inference
results.summary: Shows that ignoring topological distance and congestion makes cache-aware-only scheduling arbitrarily suboptimal; proposes a network cost oracle for decode instance selection, cutting mean TTFT by up to 21.2% and lifting SLO attainment by 20.1 points.

results.title: The same 16 GPUs, twice the users: Inference-aware routing for LLM clusters
results.summary: Details Red Hat / llm-d inference-aware routing that schedules requests based on KV-cache state, queue depth, and load, reporting up to 99% lower TTFT and 109% higher throughput versus baseline Kubernetes routing on H100 clusters.

results.title: FairBatching: Fairness-Aware Batch Formation for LLM Inference
results.summary: Identifies unfairness between prefill and decode in stall-free batching schedulers and proposes a fair dynamic batch formation algorithm that reduces TTFT tail latency by up to 2.29x while maintaining TPOT SLOs.

results.title: Argus: Token Aware Distributed LLM Inference Optimization
results.summary: Proposes a token-aware distributed edge-cloud LLM inference framework with a Length-Aware Semantics module that predicts output token lengths and a Lyapunov-guided offloading optimizer balancing prefill and decode costs.

results.title: Why goodput matters more than throughput for LLM serving
results.summary: Expert analysis arguing that goodput (requests meeting TTFT/TPOT SLOs) is the correct optimization target over raw throughput, illustrating a ~10x TPOT disparity between configs with similar throughput.
